findings.reason: The protected SQL is concise, conventional, and expert-interview ready. user_sessions names the one-row-per-active-user relation, session_count identifies its measure, and average_sessions_per_user states the output exactly. Filtering, distinct counting, user grouping, averaging, rounding, and empty-result handling appear at their natural relational grains without an unnecessary join or opaque alias; no material improvement warrants a candidate.

BETWEEN includes both 2019-06-28 and 2019-07-27 and excludes adjacent outside dates. Grouping retained events by user_id creates one row for each active user. COUNT(DISTINCT session_id) counts a session once despite duplicate rows, several dates, or different activity types and is unambiguous because every session belongs to one user. AVG gives those user rows equal weight, ROUND applies to the final average, and IFNULL converts the NULL aggregate over an empty user relation into the required zero-valued row.

Metadata consistently identifies Premium LeetCode database problem 1142, SQL/MySQL, and its SQL query entrypoint. Authenticated source evidence confirms the four Activity columns and types, duplicate-row allowance, exact activity enum, single-user session ownership, inclusive 30-day period ending 2019-07-27, at-least-one-activity qualification, per-user distinct-session average, two-decimal rounding, and exact output alias. The query preserves every one of those semantics.

The protected app-local sql.sql is byte-for-byte identical to immutable leetcode.sql bound to verified submission 2067830907. Both use the same inclusive filter, user grouping, distinct session count, derived-table alias, outer average, final rounding, null-to-zero conversion, and projection, so no adapter semantic gap or candidate replacement exists.

Filtering examines up to R rows, while grouping and distinct-session counting may sort the qualifying relation, giving the conservative logical O(R log R) time bound. The grouping and distinct state can hold O(R) values, matching the manifest's O(R) space bound; a database engine may improve physical execution with hashing or indexes.

The unchanged hidden tiers grow from 64 through 512 qualifying sessions for one user. Direct grouping scales near linearly, while the independently correct same-user self-join generates every session pair before distinct counting. The protected query passed every output and scaling at a 0.98x largest runtime ratio and -0.01 relative growth exponent. The self-join passed all 9 ordinary cases and all three benchmark outputs but failed only scaling at 64.25x and +1.22.

The Approach accurately derives early inclusive-window filtering, per-user distinct-session counts, an outer equal-weight average, one final rounding operation, and explicit empty-result conversion. Its O(R log R) time and O(R) space match the implementation and manifest, and its alternatives and edge cases cover the equivalent global ratio, slower self-join, duplicates, sessions spanning dates, inactive users, and the empty window.

The modular Reference preserves the complete Activity schema, all four enum literals, duplicate and ownership guarantees, exact date period, qualifying-session rule, active-user grain, rounding requirement, and output alias.
